$comment: DRAFT ledger for issue #60, one director only (Federico Fellini). Same schema as essential10-example.json (schemaVersion 1) with additive fields: format, tmdbYear, sightAndSound2022, rt.reason, rt.alternateCut. Not approved, not for app use until the owner signs off the method and the score-display licensing decision.
methodSummary: Eligibility (TMDB crew job Director, feature film; documentaries and co-directed films allowed where essential and flagged) -> longlist with evidence panel -> tier by directing achievement (craft, innovation, influence, canon) with IMDb and RT used only as within-source ordinal sanity checks -> order within tier by documented editorial judgement. IMDb /10 and Tomatometer % are never averaged or combined. Fewer than ten films where the work does not support ten.

imdb.source: IMDb non-commercial dataset title.ratings.tsv.gz (averageRating, numVotes), matched on IMDb title id; title ids found through title.crew.tsv.gz (director nconst) and cross-checked against TMDB by title, year and runtime
imdb.note: Live IMDb title pages were attempted first and did not return a usable page to an automated request (an empty response, not a human-readable page), so ratings come from the official daily dataset instead; this is the same fallback as the Kurosawa example. The dataset licence is personal / non-commercial use only; see licensing caveats in ESSENTIAL_10_EXAMPLE.md.

rt.source: Rotten Tomatoes film page, critics Tomatometer (scorePercent) and critic review count (reviewCount) read from the page's embedded data
rt.note: Read directly from each film's rottentomatoes.com page with a command-line fetch, one request per page. Percentages and counts are live and change; treat as a dated snapshot. Where a page shows fewer than about 5 reviews no Tomatometer is published and the value is null.

sightAndSound.source: BFI, The Greatest Films of All Time (2022 Sight and Sound poll), positions as listed on the page
sightAndSound.note: The page text was read in two halves; ranks 49-50 and the very bottom of the list were not visible in the extracted text. A film shown without a position was not seen in the portions read; that is not proof it is absent. '=' marks a tie. The page does not state 'critics' poll' in the extracted text, so the figure is labelled 'the 2022 Sight and Sound poll'.

films.title: 8½
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay, Story).
films.rationale: A film about a director's creative block that became the model for self-portrait cinema, with dream and memory moving freely through one man's day; 98% on RT and the highest-placed Fellini in the 2022 Sight and Sound poll (=31).

films.title: La Dolce Vita
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay, Story).
films.rationale: Seven nights and days of a journalist in Rome, the Palme d'Or winner (Cannes 1960) that put celebrity culture and the paparazzi on screen; 75 RT reviews at 95%.

films.title: La Strada
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay, Story).
films.rationale: The neorealist road tragedy of Gelsomina and Zampano with Nino Rota's score; the first of his Foreign Language Oscar winners and 97% from 77 reviews.

films.title: Nights of Cabiria
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay, Story).
films.rationale: Giulietta Masina's Rome prostitute whose faith survives repeated betrayal; Foreign Language Oscar winner with 100% from 41 reviews and 8.1 on IMDb.

films.title: Amarcord
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay, Story).
films.rationale: Memory of a Romagna town living under fascism, comic and elegiac; Foreign Language Oscar winner and the clearest statement of his late autobiographical mode.

films.title: I Vitelloni
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay, Story).
films.rationale: Five idle young men in a provincial town, the bridge from neorealism to his own autobiographical manner; 100% from 28 reviews.

films.title: Juliet of the Spirits
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay, Story).
films.rationale: His first full-length colour feature, a hallucinatory study of a wife's imagination with Giulietta Masina; the clearest case for his colour design.

films.title: Fellini Satyricon
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay, Story).

rt.rtYearNote: TMDB lists it as 'Satyricon'; IMDb and RT as 'Fellini Satyricon'.

films.rationale: A hallucinatory, stylised vision of ancient Rome built on constructed sets, among the most visually uncompromising films he made; mixed evidence (6.8 on IMDb, 74% on RT).

films.title: The White Sheik
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay, Story). His first solo-credited feature; Variety Lights (1950, TMDB 43389) was co-directed with Alberto Lattuada and is not ranked.
films.rationale: A farce about a bride lost in Rome chasing a photo-romance idol, showing his comic gift before the major films; evidence is thin (7,667 IMDb votes, 13 RT reviews) so it is the closest call and the reason this list is nine long.

nearMisses.title: Fellini's Roma
nearMisses.reason: A city portrait with strong passages, but RT 65% from 17 reviews and overlaps 8½'s autobiographical mode; first reserve for a tenth place.

nearMisses.title: Il Bidone (The Swindle)
nearMisses.reason: Minor work between La Strada and Nights of Cabiria.

nearMisses.title: Variety Lights
nearMisses.reason: Co-directed with Alberto Lattuada; excluded from ranking as a joint credit, and only 9 RT reviews.

nearMisses.title: And the Ship Sails On
nearMisses.reason: Late fantasy, not stronger than the nine.

nearMisses.title: Boccaccio '70 / Spirits of the Dead (anthology segments)
nearMisses.reason: Anthology segments (Toby Dammit, The Temptation of Dr. Antonio); excluded as non-features.

unverified: The RT release year on the La Dolce Vita, Fellini Satyricon and The White Sheik pages could not be parsed by the extraction script, so rtListedYear is null for them.
Variety Lights (TMDB 43389) is co-directed with Alberto Lattuada and Boccaccio '70 / Spirits of the Dead contain Fellini segments; none is ranked.

IMDb ids matched by title, year and runtime; 8½ is 139 minutes on TMDB and 138 on IMDb; La Dolce Vita 174 on both; Juliet of the Spirits is 148 on TMDB and 137 on IMDb (a single entry on both, so the gap is treated as a cut or listing difference).
TMDB year for La Dolce Vita is 1960, Amarcord 1973; the BFI page lists Amarcord as 1972 and Sight and Sound's year therefore differs by one.
